### common_raven.c1: Opportunistic thermal soaring over broken ground

Trait ← a resident scavenger must patrol a huge home range of broken terrain to find the rare carrion that is its pay ← sun heats sunlit rock, scree and cliff faces far faster than valley shade, so those slopes exhale rising thermals while cool ground does not ← so the raven flaps between lift sources and glides the legs between them, letting warm air pay for most of the climbing muscle ← F2, F6, F12

- **Skill:** Ride (Basic): while the lift indicator shows rising air, gliding legs cost 90% less stamina and the raven can commute 40 km per rest cycle, spotting carrion from 3 km mid-glide without spending a search action
- **Weakness:** no sun, no lift: under overcast or rain the indicator goes dark and range halves, and at night it is a slow flapper on the ground where anything can reach it
- **Observe:**
  1. wings held flat and motionless only while circling above sun-warmed rock
  2. a flap-flap-glide rhythm across a shaded valley, then wings lock open on the next bright slope
  3. a bird losing height over cold water and regaining it the moment it crosses a sunlit scree
- **Journal:** It buys altitude with sun on stone, and pays in muscle whenever the sun clocks off.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-18, 2026-11-18)
  - 40 km per rest cycle is plausible for dispersing juveniles but not every individual every day; tie long commute to sunny, broken terrain biomes only.
  - scores: astrobio 9, designer 9, physicist 8, skeptic 7
  - Analogue: Corvus corax — flap-glide and thermal soaring over rugged terrain; scavenger wide-ranging (Pennycuick flight energetics; raven ecology Heinrich): as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
  - Analogue: real biology behind this chain: see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own (Pennycuick 2008 [unverified])
  - Fix: 40 km per rest cycle is plausible for dispersing juveniles but not every individual every day; tie long commute to sunny, broken terrain biomes only.
- **Chain provenance:** council run `autoloop-2026-11-18`; by s, k, e, p, t, i, c

### common_raven.c2: Scatter-hoards, re-hides when watched

Trait ← hundreds of separate stores are each remembered by the landmark beside them ← a bird that was watched while hiding returns later and moves the food somewhere else ← a store is only worth having if its location stays secret from other minds ← and winter food is patchy, frozen and contested, which is what makes hiding worth the memory ← F4, F20, F29

- **Skill:** Pilfer (Signature): locates any hidden cache within 50 m, including the player's own stash, and relocates its own hoard so that scrying shows the old site
- **Weakness:** its memory is landmark-bound: move the stones and it loses its own hoard, and if it knows it is being watched it abandons a good cache, so a visible observer costs it food
- **Observe:**
  1. a bird pressing food into the ground, then looking up and around
  2. the same morsel reappearing in a different place an hour later
  3. a scatter of small pits under a shrub, most of them empty
- **Journal:** It hides food from you, then hides the hiding from you.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-18, 2026-11-18)
  - 50 m cache find is strong; frame as landmark vicinity search unless player cache has scent/sign cue. Re-hiding when watched is better documented as strategic recaching under observer risk in corvids broadly.

  - Analogue: real biology behind this chain: see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own (Heinrich 1998 [unverified]; Bugnyar 2002 [verified])
  - Fix: 50 m cache find is strong; frame as landmark vicinity search unless player cache has scent/sign cue. Re-hiding when watched is better documented as strategic recaching under observer risk in corvids broadly.

### common_raven.c3: Beak-wrestling and drop-catch juvenile play

Trait ← a long juvenile period before territory acquisition selects for extended neural plasticity and social learning ← this extended apprenticeship requires low-cost rehearsal of precise motor sequences and tolerance thresholds ← beak-wrestling and object drop-catch practice aerial tracking, grip control, and partner reliability without injury or caloric waste ← this cheap assay of coordination builds cooperative bonds for adult cache defense, though the direct survival payoff remains speculative biology ← F31, F29

- **Skill:** Play (Social): one safe turn with no damage: bonds one ally (+1 loyalty) and, as explicit game magic rather than biology, reveals one hidden item or trap within 10m; either bird may break play for 1 turn to gain alertness and a 20% speed boost for the next 2 turns
- **Weakness:** play is loud, slow and conspicuous: a playing pair is distracted and will not flee mid-game, so a stalking predator or player catches both; breaking play costs a turn, so timing it wrong still leaves an opening
- **Observe:**
  1. two birds gripping each other's beaks and pulling without injury
  2. a stick dropped, caught, carried up and dropped again, over and over
  3. a bird sliding down a snowbank and walking back up to do it again
- **Journal:** It practises being clever in public and calls it fun.
